judge.definition: A court official who oversees cases and makes legal decisions.

lawyer.definition: A professional person authorized to practice law.

prosecutor.definition: A government official who conducts criminal prosecutions on behalf of the state.

defense-attorney.definition: A lawyer representing the accused person in a criminal proceeding.

bailiff.definition: A court officer whose responsibilities may include courtroom order, security, or carrying out court instructions.

court-reporter.definition: A professional who creates an official word-for-word record of court proceedings.
court-reporter.exampleUsage: The court reporter recorded the hearing.

jury-member.definition: A person selected to serve on a jury and consider evidence in a court case.
jury-member.exampleUsage: The jury member listened to the testimony.

witness.definition: (law) a person who testifies under oath in a court of law.

clerk.definition: A court employee who maintains records and assists with court administration.

interpreter.definition: A person who conveys spoken or signed communication between languages during proceedings.

judge-s-bench.definition: The raised desk or platform where the judge sits in a courtroom.
judge-s-bench.exampleUsage: The judge sat at the judge's bench.

witness-stand.definition: An enclosed area in a courtroom where a witness gives evidence while answering questions.

jury-box.definition: A separate area in a courtroom where the members of a jury sit during a trial.

gallery.definition: The area of a courtroom where members of the public sit.

defense-table.definition: The courtroom table used by the defendant and defense legal team.
defense-table.exampleUsage: The defense attorneys organized documents at the defense table.

prosecution-table.definition: The courtroom table used by the prosecution legal team.
prosecution-table.exampleUsage: The prosecution table was opposite the defense table.

lectern.definition: Desk or stand with a slanted top used to hold a text at the proper height for a lecturer.

court-seal.definition: An official emblem or stamp used to authenticate documents issued by a court.
court-seal.exampleUsage: The certified order carried the court seal.

railing.definition: A barrier consisting of a horizontal bar and supports.

exit.definition: An opening that permits escape or release.

gavel.definition: A small mallet used by a presiding officer or a judge.

law-book.definition: A reference volume gathers statutes, written laws passed by a legislature, court decisions, and legal commentary for study and practice.

case-file.definition: The collected documents and records relating to one legal case.

evidence-bag.definition: A specialized bag or package used to contain, label, and preserve evidence for legal proceedings.
evidence-bag.exampleUsage: The sealed evidence bag had an identifying case label.

badge.definition: A worn sign or card showing a stated identity or affiliation.

handcuffs.definition: Linked metal restraints placed around a person's wrists.

oath-card.definition: A card containing the formal words or reminder used when a witness takes an oath or affirmation.
oath-card.exampleUsage: The clerk referred to the oath card before the witness testified.

subpoena.definition: A legal order requiring testimony or production of specified evidence under applicable rules.

verdict-form.definition: A court form on which a jury or judge records the formal decision on specified questions or charges.
verdict-form.exampleUsage: The jury returned the completed verdict form.

witness-list.definition: A document naming the witnesses that a party expects to call in a legal proceeding.
witness-list.exampleUsage: The attorneys exchanged the witness list before trial.

trial.definition: A court proceeding in which disputed facts or legal claims are examined and decided under the applicable rules.

hearing.definition: (law) a proceeding (usually by a court) where evidence is taken for the purpose of determining an issue of fact and reaching a decision based on that evidence.

testimony.definition: Evidence given by a witness under the required oath or affirmation.

cross-examination.definition: Questioning of a witness by the opposing side after direct testimony.
cross-examination.exampleUsage: Cross-examination began after the witness finished direct testimony.

objection.definition: (law) a procedure whereby a party to a suit says that a particular line of questioning or a particular witness or a piece of evidence or other matter is improper and should not be continued and asks the court to rule on its impropriety or illegality.

ruling.definition: A court's decision about a legal question or request.

sentence.definition: A punishment imposed by a court following a criminal conviction.

appeal.definition: A legal process requesting review of a decision by a higher court under the applicable rules, without guaranteeing a changed outcome.

acquittal.definition: A formal finding that an accused person is not guilty of the specified criminal charge.

conviction.definition: A formal finding that an accused person is guilty of a criminal offense.

contract.definition: A binding agreement between two or more persons that is enforceable by law.

warrant.definition: A written court order authorizing a specified action, such as a search or arrest.

summons.definition: An official notice requiring a person to appear or respond in a legal proceeding.
summons.arabicTranslation: إخطار بالحضور أو الرد أمام المحكمة

complaint.definition: (civil law) the first pleading of the plaintiff setting out the facts on which the claim for relief is based.

motion.definition: A formal request asking a court to make a decision or take an action.

brief.definition: A document stating the facts and points of law of a client's case.

deposition.definition: Testimony recorded outside court under oath or affirmation as part of a legal proceeding.

injunction.definition: A court order requiring a person to do, or refrain from doing, a specified act.

plea.definition: A defendant’s formal response to a criminal charge, such as guilty or not guilty, in this context.

wig.definition: Hairpiece covering the head and made of real or synthetic hair.

suit.definition: In this clothing list, a matching jacket and trousers or skirt, rather than a legal action.

tie.definition: Neckwear consisting of a long narrow piece of material worn (mostly by men) under a collar and tied in knot at the front.

briefcase.definition: A flat case with a handle for carrying documents or a laptop.

lanyard.definition: A cord worn around the neck to hold an identification card or small item.

id-badge.definition: A card or tag worn in a workplace or institution displays a person’s name, photograph, and affiliation to identify them.

pen.definition: A writing implement with a point from which ink flows.

notepad.definition: A small pad of paper used for writing quick notes.

folder.definition: A folded cover used to keep papers together.

defendant.definition: A person or institution against whom an action is brought in a court of law.

plaintiff.definition: A person who brings an action in a court of law.

jury.definition: A body of citizens sworn to give a true verdict according to the evidence presented in a court of law.

evidence.definition: (law) all the means by which any alleged matter of fact whose truth is investigated at judicial trial is established or disproved.

document.definition: A written, printed, or digital record containing information.

oath.definition: A commitment to tell the truth (especially in a court of law).

verdict.definition: (law) the findings of a jury on issues of fact submitted to it for decision.

cross-examine.definition: To question a witness for the opposing side during a legal proceeding after that witness's direct testimony.
cross-examine.exampleUsage: The defense attorney was allowed to cross-examine the witness.

deliberate.definition: To discuss or consider information carefully before reaching a decision.

robe.definition: A long loose garment worn by a judge as official courtroom dress.
